## 1. Goal

Build `aprm`, the console program: the synopsis deliverable and the tool every Python script calls. It reads `jobs.csv`, runs the chosen policy, writes `results.csv`, and optionally the log and metrics. `make test` runs every golden case through it.

## 2. Background

**From PRD §5 Console program:**

```
aprm --in jobs.csv --out results.csv [--policy fcfs|priority|sjf|aging|reserve|knapsack]
     [--cpu 16] [--mem 32768] [--alpha-milli 100] [--threshold 50] [--eps 0.1]
     [--log log.txt] [--metrics metrics.json] [--exact]
```

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 bad arguments, 2 input file error, 3 invalid job, 4 internal error. Errors go to stderr in one line, using the same names as the table above.

**From PRD §1A M6:**

| # | Feature | Owner | Done when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M6 | Console program | Krishna | `aprm --policy aging --in jobs.csv --out results.csv` works on all golden cases |

**From PRD §5 CSV formats:**

Input, `jobs.csv`, header required:

```csv
id,arrival,duration,cpu,mem,priority
1,0,30,8,20480,2
2,1,5,2,1024,7
```

Output, `results.csv`:

```csv
id,arrival,start,finish,wait,turnaround,priority,cpu,mem
1,0,0,30,0,30,2,8,20480
2,1,1,6,0,5,7,2,1024
```

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- Argument parsing for every flag in PRD §5 with defaults from `config.h`
- Reading the input file, calling `csv_read_jobs`, `sim_create` (max_jobs = 1,000,000), `sim_add_job`, `sim_step` to the end
- Writing `results.csv`, `--log` (one sentence per line), `--metrics` (metrics JSON)
- Exit codes 0–4 and one-line stderr errors
- A golden-case runner wired into `make test` (`tests/cases/<case>.<policy>.expected.csv` vs output)

**Out of scope:**

- `--exact` behaviour (K-33; until then it returns exit 1 with "exact solver not built yet")
- Policies other than FCFS working end to end (K-19, K-26, K-34)

## 5. Specification

Usage (PRD §5):

```text
aprm --in jobs.csv --out results.csv [--policy fcfs|priority|sjf|aging|reserve|knapsack]
     [--cpu 16] [--mem 32768] [--alpha-milli 100] [--threshold 50] [--eps 0.1]
     [--log log.txt] [--metrics metrics.json] [--exact]
```

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 bad arguments; 2 input file error (cannot open or read; CSV parse errors); 3 invalid job; 4 internal error (e.g. out of memory). Errors go to stderr as one line using the PRD §5 names, e.g. `PARSE_ERROR: Line 12, column cpu: not a number.`

The binary is built at `build/aprm` (D51). O-8 is decided (D54): the CLI is all-or-nothing. Jobs are added in file order; on the first `sim_add_job` failure it prints one line (`<NAME>: <message> (line N)`), exits 3 (OUT_OF_MEMORY: 4) without running, and writes no output file. The CSV reader's line numbers must therefore be carried through to the add loop. The core's LIMIT_REACHED message is generic ("Limit is N jobs."); the CLI chooses its own wording. A test must cover the exit-3 case and the missing output file; the golden runner also compares `<case>.expected.exit` and `<case>.expected.stderr` for the capacity-rejection case (K-17). `--alpha-milli` is an integer 0–10,000. The golden runner discovers every `tests/cases/<case>.<policy>.expected.csv`, runs `build/aprm --policy <policy> --in tests/cases/<case>.csv --out <tmp>` and compares byte for byte.

## 6. Step-by-step tasks

1. Write the golden runner and add it to `make test` (expect failures at first)
2. Implement argument parsing with strict integer parsing
3. Implement file reading (size-checked) and the run loop
4. Implement output writing for results, log and metrics
5. Map every error to its exit code and one stderr line
6. Test each exit code
7. Run `make sanitize` on the CLI tests

## 7. Tests to write

| Test name | What it checks | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `golden-fcfs` | Every `*.fcfs.expected.csv` | Byte-identical output |
| `exit-1` | Unknown flag; `--policy foo`; `--alpha-milli 1.5` | Exit 1, one stderr line |
| `exit-2` | Missing input file | Exit 2 |
| `exit-3` | A job larger than `--mem` | Exit 3, one stderr line with the CSV line number, and no output file written |
| `log-file` | `--log` | One sentence per decision |
| `metrics-file` | `--metrics` | Valid metrics JSON in the PRD §5 shape |

## 8. Acceptance criteria (Done when)

- [ ] `build/aprm --policy fcfs --in … --out …` matches every FCFS golden case (M6; other policies follow in K-19, K-26, K-34)
- [ ] Exit codes 0–4 exactly as PRD §5, each covered by a test
- [ ] Every error is one stderr line using the PRD §5 error name
- [ ] `make test` runs all golden cases
- [ ] `make sanitize` clean

## 9. How to verify

```sh
make && make test
build/aprm --policy fcfs --in tests/cases/fcfs_basic.csv --out /tmp/r.csv && diff /tmp/r.csv tests/cases/fcfs_basic.fcfs.expected.csv
```
A pass: `make test` reports every golden case passing and `diff` prints nothing.

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** a thin shell around the core: all file I/O and printing live here, so `core/` stays pure (hard rule 2).
**Examiner question:** "Is this the synopsis deliverable?" — Yes: C, structs, heap, greedy fill, aging, resource check, run from the console.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Reading a huge file without a size limit
- Using `atof` for `--eps` without range checks
- Exit code 0 when some jobs were rejected
- Windows line endings in expected files making diff fail
